data.narrative: The student executed a comprehensive system-level security and architecture review across all AI-generated codebase components. By combining automated discovery with rigorous manual critical-path call chain analysis, they surfaced and neutralised a critical composite privilege escalation vulnerability on member role updates, proving that isolated function reviews fail to detect vulnerabilities born from component interaction.

dimension_scores.observation: Constructed high-fidelity, 6-constraint remediation prompts specifying exact permission guards, self-modification blocks, role enums, and negative test criteria.
dimension_scores.evidence: Authored production-grade prompt in progress/ai-augmented-engineering/module-07-fix.md eliminating vague instructions.

dimension_scores.observation: Audited the complete system across 5 dimensions: authentication/authorization mappings, input validation enums, IDOR boundaries, information leakage, and concurrency.
dimension_scores.evidence: Documented 11 endpoints, 7 input fields, and 5 cross-tenant test scenarios in progress/ai-augmented-engineering/module-07-system-review.md.

dimension_scores.observation: Rapidly diagnosed how two separate medium-severity flaws (coarse-grained membership check + unvalidated role string) composed into a critical privilege escalation.
dimension_scores.evidence: Traced the 4-step exploit in progress/ai-augmented-engineering/module-07-break.md and verified complete remediation in a single pass.

dimension_scores.observation: Articulated why AI coding models structurally miss privilege escalation and contextual vulnerabilities (AI checks syntactic structure, humans check semantic intent).
dimension_scores.evidence: Explained how LLM pattern matching satisfied the literal prompt ('team member update') while violating the hierarchical security model.

dimension_scores.observation: Delivered an exhaustive living security checklist and verified 100% test pass rate across all 8 security boundary scenarios.
dimension_scores.evidence: All 8 boundary test scenarios passed (403 for viewer self-escalation, 400 for invalid role enum, 403 for cross-tenant tampering).
